$comment: Deployed Barkeep contract addresses on Stellar Testnet.
These are public on-chain identifiers, not secrets: every one of them is
already readable by anyone from the ledger, and they are useless without
the keys that authorise calls. The keys live outside the repository (see
docs/DEPLOYMENTS.md). Checking the ids in is what makes a deployment
reproducible instead of living in one person's shell history.
Testnet only. There is deliberately no mainnet file: per
docs/ARCHITECTURE-v2.md constraint 4, mainnet needs a written policy
AUDIT STATUS: none of these contracts is audited. They are written in
this repository and run on Testnet only. The OpenZeppelin audits cover
the stellar-accounts LIBRARY at v0.7.0-rc.1, four tags behind the 0.7.2
we depend on, and cover none of this code. See ARCHITECTURE-v2.md 4.1.

policyPayeeAllowlist.note: Written by Barkeep, not OpenZeppelin: stellar-accounts 0.7.2 ships no payee allowlist. Its enforce emits no event (see the crate docs).

smartAccount.adminSignerNote: Ed25519 human signer, standing in until a real passkey is registered (needs a browser; see ARCHITECTURE-v2 4.1 and 13).

token.description: TAB, a throwaway Testnet test asset issued by Barkeep's deployer. It is not USDC and has no value.
token.note: Stellar Asset Contract for TAB:<deployer>, a throwaway Testnet test asset used by the tab done-test.

doneTests.note: Each run installs a fresh agent rule with a short expiry, so rule ids and tx hashes differ per run. The hashes below are from the run recorded in the commit message.

transferOutsideTheServer.note: tab_status reflected this without being told: spent 0 -> 0.0002

x402Spike.question: Can an x402 exact payment be made FROM the smart account, authorised by the agent session key under a tab rule, and settled by a facilitator?
x402Spike.answer: Yes with a self-hosted @x402/stellar 2.25.0 facilitator (fee ceiling raised, event check narrowed to the asset contract). No through the public facilitator https://x402.org/facilitator.
x402Spike.note: Seller was a local x402 v2 server on 127.0.0.1; seller payTo and the T0 payer were fresh friendbot accounts with a TAB trustline. Successful flags, ledgers and fees cross-checked on Horizon; T4's auth entry and events read back from RPC.

T0_controlClassicPayerPublicFacilitator.envelope: fee bump: inner source GC6CSXBV4C6RL3HEDTW57KXYXSSXKAWKGYDEOSATXM3XNKXSR2VRYN3K, fee source GC5OLUZ4WANPN6VT7YGTK2SRMZG762KOVKJXHWIO4K57UBASO2FMNRET (both listed by the facilitator's /supported)

T1_stockClientSmartAccountPayer.result: threw before any request: "Failed to create payment payload: invalid version byte. expected 48, got 16"
T1_stockClientSmartAccountPayer.cause: AssembledTransaction.signAuthEntries passes the signature to authorizeEntry as raw bytes, which takes the classic-account branch and decodes the C-address as an ed25519 key

verify.invalidMessage: simulation-derived fee 324039 stroops exceeds ceiling 50000 stroops

T4_localFacilitatorFeeCeilingAndAssetEve.facilitator: same, plus validateSimulationEvents given only events emitted by the asset contract

payAndFetch.note: Real MCP tools over an in-memory transport. Seller: local x402 v2 server whose facilitator is src/facilitator.ts served over HTTP, reached through @x402/core HTTPFacilitatorClient. The deployer is the facilitator's fee payer. Tab cap 5000 base units. 12/12 checks passed. Successful flags, ledgers and fees cross-checked on Horizon; events and the refusal's contract error read back from RPC.

P2_overRemainingCapRefused.payAndFetch: refused at the enforcing simulation before anything was sent to the seller: Error(Contract, #3221) SpendingLimitExceeded; price 0.00045 <= max_amount 0.001, remaining 0.0003

forcedOnChain.how: the same transfer (4500, same seller, rule 13, agent key) submitted directly with P1's footprint, because under x402 the client and the facilitator both simulate first and an over-cap payment never reaches the ledger

rerunWithFacilitatorKey.note: Re-run 2026-09-13 after the facilitator moved to its own key (fee payer GACGJIUB...). 12/12. The record above is the original run.

demoStack.note: bin/barkeep-mcp over stdio -> src/seller.ts (persistent) -> src/facilitator.ts (own key) -> Testnet. 9/9. Sources and successful flags cross-checked on Horizon.

twoUrlsAtOnce.note: settled in consecutive ledgers: the facilitator serialises settlements

demoStack.datasetOverMaxAmount: Price 0.002 exceeds max_amount 0.001. Nothing was signed or paid.

payeeAllowlist.note: Real MCP tools over an in-memory transport; local seller on Barkeep's facilitator over HTTP; fresh throwaway payees, both with a TAB trustline. Tab cap 5000 base units, spending limit and allowlist on the SAME rule. 38/38. Every on-chain refusal code below was read back from RPC getTransaction's diagnostic events for that hash, not taken from a simulation; every successful flag, ledger and fee cross-checked on Horizon.

A2_nonAllowlistedPayeeFails.payAndFetch: refused at the enforcing simulation, nothing sent to the seller: Error(Contract, #3901) PayeeNotAllowed; price 0.0001, remaining 0.0004 (under the cap)

forcedOnChain.how: the same transfer (1000 to the unlisted payee, rule 23, agent key) submitted directly with A1's footprint

A2b_allowlistedButOverCapFails.payAndFetch: refused at the enforcing simulation: Error(Contract, #3221) SpendingLimitExceeded; price 0.00045, remaining 0.0004

agentOnTabRule.why: add_payee is a call to the policy; the tab's rule is CallContract(token)

A3_agentCannotAddPayee.agentOnRule0: refused in simulation, Error(Contract, #3002): rule 0 has no policies, so it needs its own signer

A4_noPayeesNoAllowAnyRefused.openTab: open_tab refused: no payees, and allow_any_payee is not true. An empty or absent payee list does not mean anyone. Pass payees (G... or C... addresses) to restrict who this tab can pay, enforced on chain, or allow_any_payee: true to open a tab that can pay anyone up to its cap. Nothing was sent.

emptyListForcedIntoInstall.how: add_context_rule with the allowlist and payees [], signed by the human signer, submitted with the footprint of a simulated valid install carrying the same auth nonce

A4_noPayeesNoAllowAnyRefused.honestScope: The account itself accepts a rule without the allowlist (that is what allow_any_payee builds), so refusing an ABSENT list is open_tab's; refusing an EMPTY list is also the contract's.

regressionRuns.note: Same day, after the change: tab-tools-testnet.mjs 10/10 and pay-and-fetch-testnet.mjs 13/13 (its P1 receipt check was stale since #5 and was corrected).

earlierRefusalCodesReverified.why: Chain.settle searched JSON.stringify of XDR diagnostic events for the text Error(Contract, #N), which never matches, so forced refusals reported the SIMULATION's code. Fixed in this change. The five earlier records were read back from RPC on 2026-09-14 and all match the ledger.

ttlExtension.why: Wasm and instance entries of all four contracts and the TAB token's instance were due to archive at ledgers 4764028-4764286, about 2026-09-19 18:49 UTC at 5.0 s/ledger. After archival every call fails at simulation.
ttlExtension.note: Extended to the network maximum; liveUntilLedger read back from RPC getLedgerEntries after each transaction, and each tx cross-checked on Horizon. Not covered: per-rule, per-signer and balance storage (rule 0 and the account's TAB balance live until ~5161758, about 2026-10-12), which the contracts extend as they write. The scheduled Testnet reset (2026-12-16 per developers.stellar.org) wipes all of it regardless.
